subject: FastPay: intermittent checkout congestion & SLA risk
body:
From: Joanna Li <joanna.li@fastpay.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@fastpay.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe p99 spikes affecting checkout - need immediate help

Diego —

We're seeing large p99 latency spikes and a correlated increase in 502/503 errors on our checkout endpoint starting ~08:30 PDT. This is impacting ~12% of transactions over the last 30m and causing some customers to abandon flows. We've already opened a PagerDuty incident (oncall+fastpay) but we need your team engaged — this is hitting our SLA and our COO is asking for a mitigation plan.

Attached are a sample of traces and the request payloads. Please advise next steps and an ETA for remediation.

Thanks,
Joanna Li
CTO, FastPay

----
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Li <joanna.li@fastpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes affecting checkout - need immediate help

Joanna — thanks for the heads-up and the artifacts. I'm escalating this to SRE and CS and we'll triage immediately. Initial ask: please keep the traces and any recent request-ids you can share; they speed correlation.

What we'll do in the next 15m:
- Rishi will validate whether this is queueing/backpressure or a model-level stall.
- If concurrency caps are being hit, we'll open an emergency escalation to increase caps and enable overflow routing to a compatible model variant.
- Grace/Laura will coordinate status updates and any credit/SLR requests from FastPay ops.

I'll update you within 30 minutes with a short action plan.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

----
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: FAST: FastPay triage — p99 spike, traces attached

Team — Joanna reported a 12% impact at p99 on checkout (FastPay). Traces attached in the customer email. High level ask: confirm whether this is:
1) request queueing / backlog at the serving runtime (KV cache contention, batching backlog)
2) backpressure from downstream adapters (telemetry shows elevated client-side timeouts)
3) concurrency cap hits on their dedicated pool causing prefork throttling

Immediate steps:
- Rishi: run the per-pool concurrency metric and the request queue length for FastPay pool between 08:00-09:30 PDT. Check for increase in enqueue time and number of rejected requests.
- Grace: prep a short customer-facing note that outlines mitigation steps (increase cap, route to standby model, enable temporary batching relax) and expected ETA.
- Laura: stand by for any contractual SLA exceptions or credit decisions.

Please paste commands/links in this thread.

Thanks,
Diego

----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FAST: FastPay triage — p99 spike, traces attached

Quick findings from initial pass (08:10–09:25 PDT window):
- Observed a sharp rise in per-request enqueue time for FastPay pool starting ~08:26; queue length hit ~600 requests (baseline ~40).
- Concurrency metric for their dedicated pool shows the concurrency cap was at 64 and we saw sustained bursts that saturated the headroom for ~9 minutes. Prefork throttles were triggered — requests waited on the admission queue.
- Two model-worker processes in the pool showed elevated GC/long-pause patterns; CPU usage spiked when we had the big traffic burst at 08:29.
- Error mode: 502s mapped to upstream container timeouts from our serving runtime; correlation with queueing/backpressure is strong.

Immediate mitigations performed (09:32–09:40):
- Increased per-customer concurrency cap from 64 -> 96 (temporary emergency bump).
- Enabled overflow routing to fallback model variant (smaller, quantized) for new requests to reduce per-token latency.
- Throttled very large-batch jobs from background pipelines for 30m window.

Preliminary result: p99 reduced from ~1.8s to ~420ms in the 09:35–09:45 window; error rate fell to baseline. We're still watching KV cache pressure and will collect full traces for root-cause.

Next steps:
- Follow-up trace analysis to see why worker processes had GC spikes (possible quantization/implementation regression in the recent runtime patch).
- Propose a config change: increase default emergency headroom for Dedicated pools with burst-prone customers and add an automated fallback route in policy.

I'll attach the short trace set and a capture of the pool metrics in the linked Drive folder.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Redwood Inference

----
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Li <joanna.li@fastpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@fastpay.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes affecting checkout - need immediate help

Joanna — update and next steps. TL;DR: root cause looks like request queueing due to a short burst that saturated the customer's concurrency cap and coincident worker GC pauses. Actions taken and immediate impact below.

What we did (already applied):
- Temp bumped FastPay concurrency cap 64 -> 96 (emergency)
- Enabled overflow routing to a lower-latency fallback model for new traffic
- Paused large background batches for 30m

Customer-visible result: p99 fell from ~1.8s -> ~420ms and 502 rate returned to baseline in ~10m.

Planned follow-up (today):
- Full trace correlation to isolate whether the GC pauses are due to the new runtime change we rolled last week. If so, revert that change for the affected kernel subset. (Rishi, ETA 3 hours)
- We'll propose an SLO-protective change: add dynamic headroom to Dedicated pools for customers with bursty traffic and an automatic overflow policy. (Diego/Platform PMs, ETA 2 business days for PR + config rollout)
- Grace will schedule a post-incident call with FastPay to review timeline and discuss any SLA credits.

If you want immediate mitigation beyond what we applied, we can keep the cap at 96 for a longer window while we finish RCA, or we can route all checkout traffic to the fallback for up to 2 hours. What is your preferred option?

Diego

----
From: Joanna Li <joanna.li@fastpay.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@fastpay.com>, FastPay SRE On-Call <oncall+fastpay@pagerduty.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes affecting checkout - need immediate help

Thanks Diego and team — appreciate the quick response. For now keep the cap at 96 and maintain overflow routing for checkout for 2 hours. We'll take the 2-hour risk while you finish the RCA. Please schedule the post-incident review and include expected customer impact and any credit proposal. Our COO wants a short summary once you have the RCA.

Joanna
